mainTopic: Stories about craving food. A wife's work duties and who said the ruling on maidservants. Then a new משנה on a husband's vow against marital relations, time away from home, and עונה.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. רב אשי saves מר זוטרא from a dangerous craving and shows that the king's meat had צרעת. A second story tells of a Roman who made a woman sick from craving pomegranates and then cured her. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה on a wife's work. She works with wool but not Roman flax, following רבי יהודה. The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר that she must work even if she brought a hundred maidservants. The גמרא also sorts out which rulings belong to רב מלכיו and which to רב מלכיא, and explains how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from the תנא קמא. A new משנה follows. It covers a husband who vows to keep away from his wife, how long students and workers may travel, and the schedule of עונה for each job. The גמרא gives the sources for בית שמאי and בית הלל, brings the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל on a vow with no time limit, and ends by ruling that a student may stay away as long as he wants if his wife agrees.

steps.title: רב אשי feeds מר זוטרא from the king's dish
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא goes pale from craving the food, so רב אשי puts some in his mouth. The chief butler complains that the king's meal is ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא's face went pale. רב אשי took some food with his finger and put it in his mouth. The butler said: You have ruined the king's meal!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רב אשי sees that מר זוטרא is in danger from craving the food, so he feeds him a taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strong craving for food you can smell can be dangerous, and that is why the גמרא tells these stories. רב אשי puts his friend's health first, even though it seems to spoil food meant for the king.

phrases.english: that his face went pale,
phrases.notes: This is מר זוטרא, pale from craving the dish the butler was carrying past.

phrases.english: he took some with his finger
and put it in his mouth.
He said to him: You have ruined the king's meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saving someone from the danger of craving comes first, even at the cost of the king's food.

steps.title: The soldiers ask why he did it
steps.stepSummary: The people there ask רב אשי why he did this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Why did you do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The king's people challenge רב אשי. This question sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From their point of view, he ruined the king's food. The question gives רב אשי the chance to show that the food was not fit for the king anyway.

phrases.english: They said to him: Why would you do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב אשי's action.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב אשי spoiled the king's dish.

steps.title: רב אשי blames whoever prepared the food
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the person who prepared such a dish is the one who really spoiled the king's food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Whoever makes food like this is the one who ruins the king's food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns the blame around. The food was already unfit before he touched it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He hints that something is wrong with the dish itself, so he did not ruin anything. This raises the next question: what is wrong with it?

phrases.english: He said to them:
The one who makes such a dish
is the one who ruins the king's food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the soldiers' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dish was unfit from the start, so the cook is to blame.

steps.title: He saw something bad in the meat
steps.stepSummary: They ask why, and רב אשי says he saw "something else" in the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Why? He said: I saw something else in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The soldiers press further, and רב אשי explains that the meat has a hidden problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Something else" is a polite way of naming צרעת. Now the claim is specific and can be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: "Something else", a polite way to name something unpleasant, here צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: Here דבר אחר does not mean "another explanation", as it usually does. It is a polite word for a disease, צרעת.

phrases.english: They said to him: Why?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דָּבָר אַחֵר חֲזַאי בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I saw "something else" in it.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying he saw signs of צרעת on the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי? אֲמַר לְהוּ: דָּבָר אַחֵר חֲזַאי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question with a more specific answer.

steps.title: They check and find the infection
steps.stepSummary: At first they find nothing. רב אשי points to a spot, they check there, and they find it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They checked and found nothing. He put his finger on a spot and said: Did you check here? They checked and found it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's claim is proven true when they check the exact spot he points to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first check seems to prove him wrong. His pointing to the exact place proves he really saw something, which clears him of ruining the king's meal.

phrases.english: They checked and did not find anything.
He took his finger and placed it on a spot,
and said to them: Did you check here?
They checked and found it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב אשי's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the meat really had צרעת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second check at the spot he pointed to.

steps.title: The Rabbis ask why he relied on a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רב אשי why he took the risk of counting on a miracle, that the צרעת would really be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to him: Why did you rely on a miracle?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן question how sure רב אשי could have been before acting. This sets up his final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing had been found, רב אשי would have been in serious trouble with the king. The רבנן ask what made him so confident.

phrases.english: The Sages said to him:
Why did you rely on a miracle?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: מַאי טַעְמָא סָמְכַתְּ אַנִּיסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the risk behind the action that just proved correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רב אשי knew ahead of time.

steps.title: He saw a spirit of צרעת hovering over it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that he saw a spirit of צרעת hovering over the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I saw a spirit of צרעת hovering over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that he was not guessing. He actually saw the sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not rely on a miracle. He acted on what he saw. This ends the story.

phrases.english: He said to them: I saw a spirit of צרעת
hovering over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's question and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw a clear sign, so he did not rely on a miracle.

steps.title: A Roman makes a woman sick from craving pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: A Roman asks a woman to marry him and she refuses. He eats pomegranates in front of her without sharing, and she gets sick from holding back her craving.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Roman asked a woman: Will you marry me? She said no. He brought pomegranates, peeled them and ate them in front of her. She swallowed all the painful saliva, and he gave her none until she became sick.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story about the harm craving can cause. Here the Roman causes it on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the physical damage of craving food without tasting it. It matches the danger מר זוטרא faced in the first story.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא רוֹמָאָה דַּאֲמַר לָהּ לְהַהִיא אִיתְּתָא:
phrases.english: There was a certain Roman who said to a certain woman:
Will you marry me?
She said to him: No.
He went and brought pomegranates,
peeled them and ate them in front of her.
All the saliva that pained her, she swallowed,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הַב לַהּ עַד דְּזָג לַהּ.
phrases.english: and he did not give her any until she became sick.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא רוֹמָאָה דַּאֲמַר לָהּ לְהַהִיא אִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme, the danger of craving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding back a strong craving for food can make a person physically ill.

steps.title: The Roman cures her when she agrees
steps.stepSummary: He offers to cure her if she will marry him. She agrees, and he has her spit out the saliva until something like a green leaf comes out and she is healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end he said: If I cure you, will you marry me? She said yes. He brought pomegranates, peeled them and ate them in front of her, and said: Spit out all the saliva that hurts you, spit it out! Until something like a green leaf came out of her, and she was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the cure: spitting out the saliva instead of swallowing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swallowing the craving saliva caused the sickness, and spitting it out cured it. The green-leaf-like thing that came out shows what had built up inside her.

keyTerms.meaning: A green leaf (like a palm leaf)

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories show that craving food you can see or smell is a real danger. The גמרא treats it seriously.

phrases.english: In the end he said to her:
If I cure you, will you marry me?
She said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל אַיְיתִי רֻימָּנֵי, פַּלִּי וַאֲכַל קַמַּהּ.
phrases.english: He went and brought pomegranates, peeled them and ate them in front of her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: כֹּל מַיָּא דְּצַעֲרִי לִךְ,
phrases.english: He said to her: All the saliva that pains you,
spit it out, spit it out!

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּנָפְקָא מִינַּהּ כִּי הוּצָא יַרְקָא
phrases.english: until something like a green leaf came out of her
and she was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אֲמַר לַהּ: אִי מַסֵּינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the Roman story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spitting out the craving saliva instead of swallowing it cured her.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: wool yes, flax no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's phrase "she works with wool" and infers that she must work wool but not flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And she works with wool." With wool, yes; with flax, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and draws an inference from its wording. This sets up the question of whose view this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the work a wife does for her husband and names only wool. The גמרא reads that as leaving out flax on purpose.

phrases.english: "And she works with wool."
With wool, yes; with flax, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹשָׂה בַּצֶּמֶר. בְּצֶמֶר אִין, בְּפִשְׁתִּים לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה obligates a wife to work wool, not flax.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows and answers that it is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא whose opinion explains the wool-not-flax inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every תנא agrees that flax is left out. Naming רבי יהודה tells us the משנה follows one specific view, which the next step proves.

phrases.english: Whose view is our Mishnah?
It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the inferred rule.

steps.title: The ברייתא: what a husband can and cannot require
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists tasks a husband cannot force on his wife. רבי יהודה adds that he cannot force her to work flax, because it makes the mouth smell and the lips stiff.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: He cannot force her to serve his father or his son, or to put straw before his animals, but he can force her to put straw before his cattle. רבי יהודה says: He also cannot force her to work flax, because flax makes the mouth smell and stiffens the lips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה is the one who exempts the wife from flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lists some tasks she can refuse. רבי יהודה adds flax to that list, which matches the משנה's mention of wool only. His reason is that spinning flax is harmful to her mouth and lips.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵינוֹ כּוֹפָהּ לֹא לַעֲמוֹד לִפְנֵי אָבִיו,
phrases.english: As it is taught: He cannot force her to stand and serve his father,
nor to stand and serve his son,
nor to put straw before his animals.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כּוֹפָהּ לִיתֵּן תֶּבֶן לִפְנֵי בְקָרוֹ.
phrases.english: But he can force her to put straw before his cattle.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He also cannot force her to work with flax,
because flax makes the mouth smell bad,
and stiffens the lips.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵינוֹ כּוֹפָהּ לֹא לַעֲמוֹד לִפְנֵי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the identification made in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That the wool-not-flax rule is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה exempts a wife from flax work.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a wife's work duties have limits, both for her dignity and for her health.

steps.title: This applies only to Roman flax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי יהודה's exemption to Roman flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to Roman flax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי יהודה's rule to one specific kind of flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is not about flax in general. It covers the Roman kind, which causes the harm described, so other flax may still be required.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife must work wool. According to רבי יהודה she is exempt from flax, but only Roman flax, which harms the mouth and lips.

phrases.english: And this applies only to Roman flax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יהודה's ruling.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: even with a hundred maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי אליעזר says that even if she brought a hundred maidservants into the marriage, she still must work wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Even if she brought him a hundred maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Others hold that a wife who brings maidservants is freed from her chores. רבי אליעזר says she must still do some work, wool spinning, no matter how many servants she has.

keyTerms.meaning: She brought into the marriage for him

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even if she brought him a hundred maidservants.
phrases.notes: The משנה finishes his thought: he can still make her work wool, because doing nothing leads to bad behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ הִכְנִיסָה לוֹ מֵאָה שְׁפָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife must work wool even if she brought many servants.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו, in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה, rules that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיו said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the final practical ruling on the משנה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the views in the משנה, רבי אליעזר's is the one we follow. A wife is never fully exempt from all work, even if she is wealthy.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר: even a wife with a hundred maidservants must do some work, such as spinning wool.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on a wife's work duties when she brings servants into the marriage.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Malkiyyu said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the משנה line just quoted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical law follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Sorting out rulings between רב מלכיו and רב מלכיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בריה דרב איקא lists three rulings said by רב מלכיו and three said by רב מלכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בריה דרב איקא said: the skewer, the maidservants, and the hair follicles were said by רב מלכיו. The forelock, the burnt ashes, and the cheese were said by רב מלכיא.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 15 quoted a ruling in the name of רב מלכיו, so the גמרא stops to explain that two Sages had very similar names. רבי חנינא בריה דרב איקא tells us which rulings belong to which Sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one-word label stands for a ruling found somewhere else in ש״ס. The 'maidservants' ruling is the one we just learned, that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. רבי חנינא gives it to רב מלכיו, which matches the name used in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: A roasting skewer (short label for a ruling in ביצה)
Hair follicles, small pits in the skin (label for a ruling in נדה)
Forelock, a lock of hair grown for idol worship (label for a ruling in עבודה זרה)
Burnt ashes put on a wound (label for a ruling in מכות)
Cheese of a non-Jew (label for a ruling in עבודה זרה)

steps.confusionAlert: רב מלכיו and רב מלכיא are two different people. Their names differ only in the last letter, so read them slowly.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina son of Rav Ika said:
The skewer, maidservants, and follicles
phrases.notes: These are nicknames for three rulings. 'Maidservants' is our ruling from step 15, that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: were said by Rav Malkiyu.
Forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese
were said by Rav Malkiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which Sage is meant by the name רב מלכיו used in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skewer, maidservants and follicles belong to רב מלכיו. Forelock, burnt ashes and cheese belong to רב מלכיא.

steps.title: רב פפא's general rule for telling the two Sages apart
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says rulings tied to a משנה or ברייתא belong to רב מלכיא, and independent rulings belong to רב מלכיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: rulings on a משנה or a ברייתא were said by רב מלכיא. Independent rulings were said by רב מלכיו. Your memory sign is: the משנה is a queen (מלכתא).
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another way to sort the rulings. He does not make a list. He uses a general rule based on what kind of statement it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ruling comments on a משנה or ברייתא, it is רב מלכיא's. If it is a stand-alone אמורא statement, it is רב מלכיו's. The memory sign links מלכיא to מלכתא, a queen, because the משנה is like a queen.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים left out of the משנה
Rulings of the אמוראים that stand on their own
Your memory sign, a trick to help you remember

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rulings on a משנה or a ברייתא were said by Rav Malkiya.
Independent rulings were said by Rav Malkiyu.
And your memory sign: the משנה is a queen.
phrases.notes: The word מַלְכְּתָא sounds like מַלְכִּיָּא, so the 'queen' משנה goes with רב מלכיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to sort the rulings than the list in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Statements on a משנה or ברייתא belong to רב מלכיא. Independent statements belong to רב מלכיו.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two approaches?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי חנינא and רב פפא actually disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. It wants to know which ruling the two approaches would assign differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two approaches seem to agree on most of the rulings. So the גמרא looks for a case where they lead to different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares step 16 with step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling would רבי חנינא and רב פפא assign to different Sages?

steps.title: They differ about the maidservants ruling
steps.stepSummary: The two approaches differ about who said the ruling on maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the ruling about maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the only real difference is our ruling about maidservants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא says the maidservants ruling was said by רב מלכיו. That ruling decides a מחלוקת in a משנה, so by רב פפא's rule it belongs to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר comes from רב מלכיו according to רבי חנינא, and from רב מלכיא according to רב פפא.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: maidservants.
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 15 about רבי אליעזר's view in our משנה. Since it rules on a משנה, רב פפא would give it to רב מלכיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ only about the maidservants ruling: רב מלכיו according to רבי חנינא, רב מלכיא according to רב פפא.

steps.title: Isn't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה and asks how his view differs from the תנא קמא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, and so on. But that is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It challenges the idea that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is adding anything new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that a wife must not sit idle. They only give different reasons: the תנא קמא says idleness leads to immorality, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it leads to madness. If the result is the same, why does the משנה need both statements?

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as the first Tanna
And so on (the rest of the quote is assumed)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, and so on.
phrases.notes: In the משנה he says that even a man who vows his wife may do no work must divorce her, because idleness leads to madness.

phrases.english: That is the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא here is רבי אליעזר, who said idleness leads to immorality.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about names and returns to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both תנאים require the wife to keep busy. Different reasons with the same result seem to make his statement extra.

steps.title: The difference: a wife who plays with small dogs or games
steps.stepSummary: The two תנאים differ when the wife keeps busy with small pets or board games.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when she plays with small puppies or with games.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a real case where the two views give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she plays with pets or games, her mind is busy, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's worry about madness does not apply. But play like this can still lead to immorality, so according to the תנא קמא she still must do real work.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא worries about immorality and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about madness. The difference shows up when the wife keeps busy only with pets or games.

phrases.english: The difference between them is
where she plays with small puppies
or with board games.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּמִיטַּלְּלָא בְּגוּרְיָיתָא קִיטָנְיָיתָא וְנַדְרְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים seem to say the same thing with different reasons.
steps.terutzMaskana: When she is busy with pets or games, there is no worry of madness but there is still a worry of immorality, so the תנא קמא would still require real work.

steps.title: A husband who vows to keep away from his wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on a husband who forbids marital relations by a נדר: בית שמאי allow two weeks and בית הלל allow one week.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man makes a vow that forbids his wife from marital relations with him, בית שמאי say this may last two weeks, and בית הלל say one week.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a husband who uses a vow to keep himself away from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two schools argue about how long the wife has to put up with this situation. בית שמאי give two weeks and בית הלל give only one. The גמרא will soon ask where each number comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: One who uses a vow to forbid something on someone

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who vows to forbid his wife
from marital relations,
Beit Shammai say: two weeks.
phrases.notes: Here שבת means a full week, not just the day of שבת.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִתַּשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya about the wife's duties ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's נדר forbidding relations may last two weeks according to בית שמאי, and one week according to בית הלל.

steps.title: How long students and workers may travel away
steps.stepSummary: Students may leave home to learn תורה for thirty days without permission. Workers may leave for one week.
steps.simpleTranslation: Students may go away to learn תורה without permission for thirty days. Laborers may go away for one week.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with related rules. It says how long a husband may be away from home without asking his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time allowed depends on the reason for the trip. Learning תורה gets a longer allowance, thirty days. Ordinary work gets only one week.

phrases.english: Students may go out to learn Torah
without permission for thirty days.
phrases.notes: He means without their wives' permission.

phrases.english: Laborers, one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתַּלְמִידִים יוֹצְאִין לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a related rule about time away from the wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Students may be away thirty days without permission. Workers may be away one week.

steps.title: The תורה's schedule of marital duty for each job
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר lists how often a husband must be with his wife, depending on his occupation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עונה mentioned in the תורה: men of leisure, every day. Laborers, twice a week. Donkey drivers, once a week. Camel drivers, once in thirty days. Sailors, once in six months. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the Torah's duty of עונה. It lists how often a husband must be with his wife, according to his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty follows how available the husband really is. The more his work keeps him away from home, the less often he must be with his wife. This list is the opinion of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The set schedule of a husband's marital duty
Men of leisure who don't work

phrases.english: The set interval stated in the Torah:
phrases.notes: שמות 21:10

phrases.english: Men of leisure: every day.
Laborers: twice a week.
Donkey drivers: once a week.
Camel drivers: once in thirty days.
Sailors: once in six months.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with the general schedule of עונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the Torah's עונה depends on occupation, from every day for men of leisure to once in six months for sailors.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three sets of numbers: how long a נדר may last, how long a husband may travel, and how often עונה is owed.

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי say two weeks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind בית שמאי's two weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking where בית שמאי get their number of two weeks. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number in the משנה must come from somewhere in the Torah. The גמרא wants to find the source for בית שמאי, and then for בית הלל.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first ruling of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for בית שמאי's two-week limit.

steps.title: Two weeks from a girl's birth, one week from a boy's
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn from a mother who gives birth to a girl, who is forbidden for two weeks. בית הלל learn from a mother who gives birth to a boy, who is forbidden for one week.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from a woman who gave birth to a girl. And בית הלל? They learn it from a woman who gave birth to a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each school bases its number on how long a new mother is forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a girl is born, the mother is forbidden for two weeks. After a boy, she is forbidden for one week. Since the Torah itself requires this much time apart, that much time is not too hard on the wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth to a girl
A woman who gave birth to a boy

phrases.english: They learn it from a woman who gave birth to a girl.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5. She is forbidden for two weeks.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
They learn it from a woman who gave birth to a boy.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2. She is forbidden for one week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question and adds the source for בית הלל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי learn from יולדת נקבה (two weeks). בית הלל learn from יולדת זכר (one week).

steps.title: Why don't בית הלל also learn from a girl's birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: if they learn from a woman after birth, they should use the longer case of a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית הלל should also learn it from a woman who gave birth to a girl!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בית הלל's source. Both cases are about a mother after birth, so why pick the shorter one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah shows that two weeks apart can be required, in the case of a girl's birth. So if the source is childbirth, two weeks should be acceptable. בית הלל's choice of one week looks unexplained.

phrases.english: But Beit Hillel should also
learn it from a woman who gave birth to a girl!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָמֵי נִגְמְרוּ מִיּוֹלֶדֶת נְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source just given for בית הלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית הלל learn from יולדת זכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If childbirth is the model, the girl case proves that two weeks is acceptable, so choosing the shorter boy case makes no sense.

steps.title: בית הלל really learn from נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the challenge works if the source were childbirth. Really, בית הלל learn from נדה, which lasts seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they learned it from a woman after birth, that is true. But בית הלל learn it from נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and changes בית הלל's source. They learn from נדה, not from a woman after birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman after birth is an unusual case, while נדה is the regular, monthly time apart. The תורה's time for נדה is seven days, so בית הלל set one week as the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period, forbidden for seven days

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not defend the earlier claim that בית הלל learn from יולדת זכר. It drops that claim and gives a new source: נדה.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's two weeks come from יולדת נקבה. בית הלל's one week comes from נדה.

phrases.english: If they learned it from a woman after birth,
that would indeed be so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל מִנִּדָּה גָּמְרִי לַהּ.
phrases.english: but Beit Hillel learn it from a menstruating woman.
phrases.notes: By Torah law, a נדה is forbidden for seven days, which matches one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִיּוֹלֶדֶת גָּמְרִי לַהּ הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by giving בית הלל a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the challenge and replaces the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בית הלל learn from יולדת זכר.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל learn from נדה, so their limit is seven days.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows each side's source and asks what principle makes them choose different sources. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 we learned that בית שמאי learn from childbirth (a girl) and בית הלל learn from נדה. The גמרא wants the reason behind that choice: why does each side think its source is the better comparison?

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the underlying principle)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the sources given in steps 26 and 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical principle that leads בית שמאי to learn from childbirth and בית הלל to learn from נדה.

steps.title: Common case versus a case he caused
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל compare a common situation to a common situation (נדה). בית שמאי compare something the husband caused to something else he caused (childbirth).
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: learn something common from something common. The other master holds: learn something he causes her from something else he causes her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the principle behind each side's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say a vow against relations happens often, and נדה also happens often, so נדה is the right comparison. בית שמאי say the husband brought on the vow himself, just as he brought on the childbirth, so childbirth is the better match. נדה is not caused by him at all.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מִידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ מִמִּידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ,
phrases.english: One master holds: learn something common from something common,
phrases.notes: This first opinion is בית הלל. A vow is common, and so is נדה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מִידֵּי דְּהוּא גָּרֵים לַהּ
phrases.english: and the other master holds: learn something that he causes her
phrases.notes: This is בית שמאי. The husband brought on the vow himself.

phrases.english: from something else that he causes her.
phrases.notes: He is the one who made her pregnant, so the childbirth also comes from him.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל = common from common (נדה, 1 week). בית שמאי = caused by him from caused by him (birth of a girl, 2 weeks).
steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: מִידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ מִמִּידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל compare by how common the case is. בית שמאי compare by whether the husband caused the situation.

steps.title: רב and שמואל on a vow with no set time
steps.stepSummary: רב says the argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about a vow with a stated time limit. With no time limit, everyone agrees he must divorce her right away. שמואל says that even then he should wait, because he may find a way to undo the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The argument is about a husband who stated a time limit. But if he made the vow with no time limit, everyone agrees he must divorce her immediately and pay her כתובה. שמואל said: Even with no time limit he should wait, because maybe he will find an opening to undo his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב and שמואל argue about how far the waiting periods of בית שמאי and בית הלל apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reasons that a vow with no end leaves her suffering with no limit from the very start, so there is no point in waiting. שמואל reasons that a חכם may still find a פתח to cancel the vow, so we give it the same waiting time first.

keyTerms.meaning: He states a specific time limit for the vow
An opening (a reason) that lets a חכם undo his vow

steps.confusionAlert: רב's 'everyone agrees' means both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree. It does not mean that שמואל agrees, and in fact he argues.

phrases.english: רב said: The argument is where he stated a time limit,
but where it is unspecified, everyone agrees
he must divorce her immediately and give her the כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּסְתָם נָמֵי יַמְתִּין,
phrases.english: And שמואל said: Even when unspecified, he should also wait,
for perhaps he will find an opening to undo his vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the waiting periods to the question of when those periods apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the waiting periods apply only to a vow with a time limit, and a vow with no time limit means immediate divorce. שמואל: even a vow with no time limit gets the waiting period.

steps.title: Didn't they already argue about this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב and שמואל already argued in the same words about a husband who vows that his wife may not benefit from him. So why is the argument repeated here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once! As we learned: If a man vows that his wife may not benefit from him, for up to thirty days he appoints a provider; for more than that, he divorces her and gives the כתובה. And רב said: This was taught only where he stated a time limit, but with no time limit, he divorces her immediately and gives the כתובה. And שמואל said: Even with no time limit he should wait, perhaps he will find an opening to undo his vow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for step 31 by quoting an identical מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about a different vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case there is a vow against benefit (support), and the case here is a vow against relations. Since רב and שמואל said exactly the same things there, it seems pointless to record their argument twice.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow that forbids something to someone else
A provider who supports her in his place
They taught this only in a case of

phrases.english: But they already argued about this once,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִלֵּיהָנוֹת לוֹ,
phrases.english: as we learned: One who vows that his wife may not benefit from him,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later in this מסכת (דף 70a).

phrases.english: up to thirty days, he must appoint a provider,
more than that, he must divorce her and give her the כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְפָרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: And רב said: They taught this only where he stated a time limit,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּסְתָם — יוֹצִיא לְאַלְתַּר וְיִתֵּן כְּתוּבָּה.
phrases.english: but where it is unspecified, he must divorce her immediately and give the כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּסְתָם נָמֵי יַמְתִּין,
phrases.english: And שמואל said: Even when unspecified, he should also wait,
for perhaps he will find an opening to undo his vow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the statement of step 31 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to record the רב and שמואל מחלוקת about a vow against relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The very same מחלוקת, in the same words, already appears about a vow against benefit, so recording it again seems repetitive.

steps.title: Both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: Both records are needed. With only the relations case, we might think רב agrees with שמואל about support, since a provider can step in there. With only the support case, we might think שמואל agrees with רב about relations, where no provider can help.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it were said only about this case (relations), we would say רב rules this way here because a provider cannot help. But in that case (support), where a provider can help, we might say he agrees with שמואל. And if it were said only about that case, we would say שמואל rules this way there, but here we might say he agrees with רב. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a צריכא: each record teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a vow against support, a פרנס can cover for the husband, so waiting costs her less. With a vow against relations, nobody can fill his place, so waiting hurts her more. Because the cases differ, recording both shows that רב and שמואל each hold their view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (each source teaches something new)
For if it had been said
It can be handled by a provider

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא shows why a ruling must be stated in two cases. Here, a provider can step in for support but not for relations, so either רב or שמואל might have changed his view.

phrases.english: It is necessary, for if it had been said only about this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the vow against marital relations from our משנה.

phrases.english: we would think that in this case רב says it
because it is impossible to use a provider,
but in that case, where a provider is possible,
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the vow against benefit, where someone else can support her.

phrases.english: I might say he agrees with שמואל.
And if it had been said only about that case,
we would think that in that case שמואל says it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָא — אֵימָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַב,
phrases.english: but in this case, I might say he agrees with רב,
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each of the two cases has its own reason that could have changed the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without both records, רב might agree to wait in the support case (a provider helps), or שמואל might agree to immediate divorce in the relations case (no provider can help).
steps.terutzMaskana: רב and שמואל each hold their view in both cases, so both records are needed.

steps.title: How long may a student go away if his wife agrees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about students leaving home to learn תורה and asks how long they may stay away when they have their wife's permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Students may leave home to learn תורה, and so on.' If they go with permission, for how long may they go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks a simple question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a limit of thirty days for a student who leaves without his wife's permission. So the גמרא wonders whether there is also a limit when she does give permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave home to go learn תורה
'And so on'. The rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: The students may leave to learn Torah, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. It allows them to leave without their wives' permission for up to thirty days.

phrases.english: With permission, for how long?
phrases.notes: He means with the wife's permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רב and שמואל on vows. It opens a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a time limit for a student who leaves to learn with his wife's permission.

steps.title: As long as he wants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that with permission there is no limit. He may go for as long as he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. If the wife agrees, the student may stay away as long as he likes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirty-day limit protects a wife who did not agree to his leaving. Once she gives permission, there is nothing to protect her from. The answer is said with surprise, as if to say: why would anyone think there is a limit?
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a new limit. It means there is no limit at all when the wife agrees.

phrases.english: As long as he wants.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With the wife's permission there is no time limit. He may go for as long as he wants.
